thread.title: Stocks Open Lower, Wal-Mart Props Dow; Bitcoin Rebounds

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Open Lower, Wal-Mart Props Dow; Bitcoin Rebounds
text:
Stocks slipped out of the starting gate Thursday's open, as analyst moves and earnings news factored into early trade, and the budget standoff in Washington gnawed at investor confidence.
X The Dow Jones industrial average launched a fraction in the red, with gains by Wal-Mart ( WMT ) bolstering early trade. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite each dipped 0.1%, as Apple ( AAPL ) posted a modest early gain and the four FANG stock tech leaders were mixed. Security software developer Symantec ( SYMC ) dropped 4% at the open, the worst loss among Nasdaq 100 stocks, following a downgrade to underperform, from hold, by Jefferies.
Markets had an eye on Washington, where federal lawmakers remained at loggerheads over a budget agreement ahead of a deadline that would shut down all non-essential government offices Friday at midnight. A stop-gap spending measure that would temporarily fund the government through Feb. 15 is set for a House vote today, though early news reports declared Republicans did not have enough support to pass the measure.
Wal-Mart, Apple, Taiwan Semi In Buy Ranges Wal-Mart was the early powerhouse among blue chips, up nearly 2% after Goldman Sachs upgraded the stock to buy, from neutral, and added the name to its Americas Conviction List. Goldman sees both Wal-Mart and the general retail environment as benefiting from recent federal tax changes. And the retailer remains "still very much in control of its own destiny," Goldman's note said, despite online disruptions to traditional retail business models.
Wal-Mart shares remained in a buy range, above a 100.23 buy point in a second-stage flat base.
Apple opened ahead 0.2%. The stock made its most decisive move to date above a 176.34 buy point Wednesday — a buy point it has been attempting to clear and hold since mid-December. Shares received a boost after the company said it would make $38 billion in repatriation tax payments, implying plans to ship home its $252 billion in overseas cash . The company also announced plans to contribute $350 billion to the U.S. economy over the next 5 years and add 20,000 new U.S. workers, among other measures.
Early earnings results rolled in, with Morgan Stanley ( MS ) and Signature Bank of New York ( SBNY ) posting narrow gains, and Bank of New York Mellon ( BK ) falling hard after early reports.
Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ) climbed 2.4% at the open. The chip foundry reported fourth-quarter revenue and earnings above analysts targets, but provided first-quarter revenue guidance below consensus views. The stock was approaching the top of a buy range, after clearing a 42.67 buy point in a cup-with-handle base Wednesday, in modest trade.
Alcoa ( AA ) tumbled, down 7.2% after missing both revenue and earnings estimates in its fourth-quarter report delivered late Wednesday. Drought in Brazil and price inflation in Spain cut into the quarter's performance, the company said. The decline left shares less than 5% above a 50.41 buy point from a late-December breakout.
Housing Starts Slip, Permits Rise; Philly Fed Survey Dives Thursday's economic news got off to a mixed start, with December housing starts slowing to an annualized rate of 1.192 million, according to Commerce Department estimates. That was down from a pace of 1.297 million starts in November, as well as forecasts for a more mild slowdown, to 1.280 million starts.
Building permits, which gauge upcoming activity, rose to 1.302 million, on an annualized basis. That was up from permits issued at a rate of 1.298 million in November, and slightly better than consensus projections for a 1.3 million permit pace.
First-time unemployment claims dropped sharply, to 220,000 claims, down nearly 16% in the week ended Jan. 13, according to the Labor Department. That was the first decline in five weeks, and far better than economist expectations for a decline to 250,000.
Manufacturing activity slowed sharply in the mid-Atlantic region, sending the Philadelphia Federal Reserve's Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey to 22.2 for January, down from 27.9 in December and undercutting consensus views for a reading of 25. January's reading was the index's lowest in five months.
IBM ( IBM ), Canadian Pacific ( CP ) and American Express ( AXP ) are among the companies expected to report after today's close.
Bitcoin, Blockchain Stocks Bounce Back Bitcoin rebounded to trade near $11,700, up 19% from Wednesday's low.
